input.rationale: This is a transfer and servicing agreement with no software, deliverables or licensed technology, so the software-conformance element has no subject matter here; the performance bargain sits at the fallback and we would not redline it. (1) Services standard: Section 3.2(a) requires Cellco to "manage, service, administer and collect on the Receivables with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables that it services for itself or others according to the Servicing Procedures", and Section 6.1(a) repeats the Servicer's representations and warranties, including compliance with Law applicable to the servicing and that "It has complied in all material respects with the Servicing Procedures with respect to the Receivables", as of the Closing Date and as of each Acquisition Date, expressly surviving transfer — coverage for the life of the deal, well beyond the 30-day fallback floor. (2) Repair/replacement: Section 3.3(b) gives us a notice-and-correct mechanic (quoted), and Section 7.2(a)(ii) allows removal and replacement of the Servicer for any unperformed obligation having a material adverse effect that is uncured after ninety (90) days. (3) Refund: Sections 2.5 and 3.3(d) require the Originator or Servicer to reacquire/acquire the affected Receivables by remitting the Acquisition Amount — the economic equivalent of a refund for non-conforming assets. Notably, there is no "AS IS" or blanket warranty disclaimer anywhere, so the walk-away position is not in play; the only no-warranty language (Section 3.3(e)) runs in our favour, being a transfer by the Issuer without recourse or warranty. Short of preferred, and noted rather than flagged: there is no express "professional and workmanlike" or no-malicious-code warranty, and the reacquisition/acquisition remedies are expressed as sole remedies (Sections 2.5(c), 3.3(g)). The separate liability floor of willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in Section 6.2(a) is a limitation-of-liability point and is left to that rule rather than flagged twice here.
